The manipulation of time in the story is exceptionally well-balanced and serves the thematic focus on institutional bureaucracy and slow-moving decay. The author compresses an entire year—from one October to the next—into a short narrative by using month-by-month markers to chronicle the agonizingly slow progress of the building's repairs. This compression effectively conveys the drawn-out, repetitive nature of the administrative delays without boring the reader. At the same time, the narrative slows down to focus on brief, specific moments—such as a grocery bag of books splitting in the hallway, a short exchange with a consultant, or the sound of a drill interrupting a seminar. This interplay between compressed months and stretched, specific interactions allows the reader to feel both the exhausting length of the ordeal and the immediate, day-to-day absurdities faced by the faculty.
